issues.body:
The test asserts only the ABSENCE of [x, p, x] and [y, p, y]. Because the reasoner has no owl:ReflexiveProperty handling at all (grep finds the symbol only in this new test), both assertions hold trivially today, and they would continue to hold even if materialize_owl_rl regressed into a complete no-op or panicked-and-recovered into returning the input unchanged. In other words, the test pins the intended guard but cannot distinguish "OWL-RL correctly declines to add reflexive edges" from "OWL-RL did nothing at all".

This is a real but low-severity gap: the test still has value as a regression guard against someone later adding a ReflexiveObjectProperty rule that does not belong in the RL profile, and it does not produce a false green for any behavior that is currently implemented. Flagging it as minor rather than major because the companion test in the same commit (sameas_and_inverse_functional) does exercise the production path and was confirmed mutation-red.
issues.title: reflexive_property_does_not_materialize_self_edges is a pure negative assertion with no positive control

verdict.summary:
Test-only change adding two unit tests to crates/sparq-reason/src/owl.rs. No production code is touched, so the only review question is whether the tests are valid and non-vacuous.

Verified empirically at the PR head:
- Both new tests pass: `cargo test -p sparq-reason --lib` (144 passed) and with the opt-in `substrate-join` feature (151 passed). Green in BOTH feature states, which matters because prp-ifp has cfg-gated default (FxHashMap `inc`) and substrate-join (`adj.probe_inc`) branches.
- Mutation spot-check on `sameas_and_inverse_functional`: disabling the production prp-ifp guard (`if ax.inv_functional.contains(&p)` -> `if false && ...`) turns the test RED at owl.rs:2310 with "prp-ifp sameAs". The test is genuinely non-vacuous and exercises the real production path, not a mock. The mutation was reverted; the working tree is clean.
- The `has()` helper fails closed (returns false when an IRI is absent from the dict), so assertions cannot pass by looking up nonexistent terms.
- Both asserted triples (`ex:a owl:sameAs ex:b`, `ex:b ex:p ex:marker`) are obtainable only via prp-ifp followed by eq-rep; nothing else in the input yields them.
- The OWL 2 RL claim in the second test is accurate: ReflexiveObjectProperty is excluded from the RL profile and `owl:ReflexiveProperty` is the correct vocabulary term. Grep confirms the reasoner has no ReflexiveProperty handling, so no-self-edges is the correct expectation.
- Style note checked and dismissed: the new `format!("{}sameAs", OWL)` differs from the neighbouring `format!("{OWL}sameAs")`, but identical const-path patterns already exist widely (sparq-reason-dl/src/extract.rs, sparq-reason-el/src/extract.rs) under a green `clippy -D warnings` gate.

One minor test-validity weakness noted below (negative test lacks a positive control). Not blocking.
